title: Apply WebSocket write deadlines under the write lock
description:
## Summary

`wsConn.SetWriteDeadline` races with a concurrent `wsConn.Write`. Gorilla's
`Conn.SetWriteDeadline` is a bare unsynchronised field assignment, and the
write path reads that field without a lock, so the two calls touch the same
memory from different goroutines with no happens-before between them.

## Affected code

- `conn_ws.go:376-382` — `SetWriteDeadline` calls `c.ws.SetWriteDeadline(t)` and
  `c.userDeadline.Store(...)` without taking `writeMu`.
- `conn_ws.go:296-305` — `writeMessage` holds `writeMu` and calls
  `c.ws.SetWriteDeadline` on the same conn.
- gorilla v1.5.3 `conn.go:787-790` — `SetWriteDeadline` is `c.writeDeadline = t`
  and nothing else; `conn.go:621` and `conn.go:748` read `c.writeDeadline` from
  the write path.

There is also a lost-update on `userDeadline`: `writeMessage` reads it at
`conn_ws.go:300` outside the setter's critical section, so a deadline set
concurrently with a write can be observed inconsistently with the socket
deadline it is supposed to suppress.

## Impact

A genuine data race for any caller that sets a write deadline from a goroutine
other than the one writing — a normal pattern for a `net.Conn`. No current test
exercises it, which is why `-race` is green today. The read side no longer has
this problem: the pump owns gorilla's read side outright.

## Proposed fix

Hold the caller's write deadline in a `wsConn` field guarded by `writeMu`, and
apply it to the socket inside `writeMessage` under that lock. `SetWriteDeadline`
then only records intent, which also removes the `userDeadline` lost-update
because the field and its use become one critical section.

Note this does not make a fired write deadline recoverable, and should not try
to: a timed-out write has already put a partial frame on the wire. Gorilla's own
documentation says the connection is corrupt afterwards. See the separate task
on interrupting an in-flight write.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test that calls `SetWriteDeadline` concurrently with `Write` passes under
  `-race`.
- `WriteTimeout` still applies its default only when the caller has not set a
  deadline, and `TestWSWriteTimeoutUnblocks` still passes.
- No change to the terminal behaviour of a fired write deadline.
